parts.markdown:
Use our free **Hawaii paycheck calculator** to estimate your take-home pay after federal income tax, Hawaii income tax, Social Security, Medicare, applicable temporary disability insurance and employee healthcare deductions.

Enter your annual salary or hourly earnings, select your pay frequency and customize your withholding information to see how much money you could receive on payday.

Hawaii has several distinctive payroll requirements, making it important to use a calculator that considers more than ordinary federal and state income taxes.

Whether you work in Honolulu, Hilo, Kailua-Kona, Kahului or another Hawaiian community, understanding your estimated net earnings can help you manage the state's household living expenses.

## How to Use the Hawaii Paycheck Calculator

If your pay stub lists Hawaii temporary disability and applicable healthcare contributions, include the amount under other deductions. Enter each deduction once.

Select annual salary or hourly wages based on your employment arrangement.

Enter your gross earnings before taxes and choose your payment frequency. Enter federal and Hawaii income tax withheld for the pay period from your pay stub.

Include health insurance premiums, retirement contributions and other employee benefits.

Review your estimated net paycheck alongside the individual deduction amounts.

Use your most recent payroll statement to confirm which deductions apply. Some employers pay the full cost of certain insurance programs, while others share the cost with employees.

## How Hawaii State Income Tax Works

Hawaii uses a progressive individual income tax system.

Different portions of taxable income may be subject to different rates, meaning your highest marginal rate should not be applied to your entire gross salary.

Hawaii has introduced tax reforms that gradually increase standard deductions and change income tax thresholds.

These reforms involve updates to payroll withholding schedules through 2031.

Consequently, a paycheck estimate based on an older tax-year configuration may overstate or understate the amount deducted from your wages.

Employers should use the appropriate version of Booklet A, Hawaii's Employer's Tax Guide.

The [Hawaii Department of Taxation payroll updates](https://tax.hawaii.gov/payrollupdate/) provide official information about annual withholding changes.

## Understanding Hawaii Form HW-4

Hawaii employees generally use Form HW-4 to provide their state withholding information.

This state certificate is separate from federal Form W-4.

The number of withholding allowances and any applicable additional withholding can influence the amount deducted from each paycheck.

If you change jobs, get married or experience a significant change in household income, review your state and federal withholding certificates.

Employers follow the state's authorized payroll calculation methods rather than simply dividing a general annual tax estimate by the number of pay periods.

Visit the official [Hawaii employer withholding resources](https://tax.hawaii.gov/geninfo/a2_b2_4empl_whhold/) for forms and calculation guidance.

## Hawaii Temporary Disability Insurance

Hawaii's Temporary Disability Insurance program, commonly called TDI, provides financial assistance to eligible employees experiencing qualifying disabilities that are not work-related.

Employers may cover the entire insurance premium or share the cost with eligible employees.

However, the employee contribution is subject to important limits.

The 2026 maximum weekly employee deduction is $7.50. An employee's contribution also cannot exceed half the premium cost or 0.5% of weekly wages.

Therefore, $7.50 is a maximum, not an automatic deduction for every Hawaii employee.

### Hawaii TDI contribution examples

Assuming the insurance premium is sufficient to allow the maximum wage-based employee share:

Suppose your weekly wages are $1,000 but the total weekly insurance premium is only $6.

Half the premium is $3, which is lower than the $5 wage-based limit. The maximum allowable employee deduction in this example would therefore be $3.

Visit the [Hawaii Temporary Disability Insurance guidance](https://labor.hawaii.gov/dcd/frequently-asked-questions/tdi/) for information about employer coverage and employee contributions.

## Understanding Hawaii Prepaid Health Care Contributions

Hawaii's Prepaid Health Care framework requires qualifying employers to provide healthcare coverage to eligible employees.

Employee premium contributions are subject to statutory limits.

For ordinary required employee coverage, the employee share generally cannot exceed half the applicable premium or 1.5% of monthly wages, whichever is lower.

For example, suppose an eligible employee earns $4,000 per month and the applicable monthly health insurance premium is $300.

Half the premium is $150.

The wage-based employee contribution limit is:

$4,000 × 0.015 = $60

The maximum employee share under these assumptions is therefore $60.

Additional dependent coverage and other voluntary benefit arrangements may require separate treatment.

The [Hawaii Department of Labor and Industrial Relations](https://labor.hawaii.gov/dcd/) provides official disability insurance and prepaid healthcare resources.

Use the actual deduction shown on your pay stub when it is available rather than automatically assuming the maximum contribution.

## Federal Taxes Deducted From Hawaii Paychecks

Hawaii employees remain subject to applicable federal income tax withholding.

The amount withheld depends on earnings, federal filing status, pay frequency and Form W-4 adjustments.

Social Security generally applies at 6.2% of covered employee wages up to the annual taxable wage ceiling of $184,500 in 2026.

Ordinary Medicare withholding is 1.45% of covered wages.

Additional Medicare withholding may apply when covered wages paid by an employer exceed $200,000 during the calendar year.

Federal payroll contributions are separate from Hawaii's income tax, disability insurance and healthcare requirements.

Review the [IRS federal withholding methods](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15t) and [Employer's Tax Guide](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15) for further information.

## Hawaii Paycheck Example: $62,400 Salary

Consider a Hawaii employee earning $62,400 annually.
Assume the employee receives $1,200 weekly, all wages are subject to ordinary federal payroll contributions and the employer deducts the maximum applicable wage-based TDI contribution.

Approximately $1,102.20 remains before federal income tax, Hawaii income tax, healthcare deductions and other employee contributions.

The disability insurance deduction could be lower if the actual premium is insufficient to support the maximum or the employer pays more of the cost.

This example illustrates selected payroll contributions, not a complete paycheck estimate.

## Hawaii Hourly Paycheck Calculator

Hourly employment is common in Hawaii's hospitality, tourism, healthcare and construction industries.

Suppose an employee earns $27 per hour and works 40 regular hours plus six qualifying overtime hours at time-and-a-half.

Regular earnings:

$27 × 40 = $1,080

Overtime earnings:

$27 × 1.5 × 6 = $243

Total gross earnings:

$1,323

Applicable state income tax, federal taxes and insurance contributions are calculated using their respective taxable wage amounts.

Some employees also receive tips, commissions or shift differentials. These earnings may affect both withholding and payroll contribution calculations.

Consult the [US Department of Labor overtime guidance](https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/overtime) for information about overtime eligibility.

## Does Hawaii Have Local Employee Income Taxes?

Hawaii counties generally do not impose a separate municipal personal wage income tax.

However, Hawaii residents may encounter other state and local taxes through their spending and household expenses.

The state's general excise tax is a business tax and should not automatically be treated as a personal wage tax deducted from ordinary employee paychecks.

Independent contractors and business owners may have different tax responsibilities from W-2 employees.

Our Hawaii paycheck calculator focuses on ordinary employee earnings rather than self-employment or business tax obligations.

## Comparing Salaries Across the Hawaiian Islands

A salary that provides a comfortable standard of living in one community may offer different purchasing power elsewhere.

Housing costs, groceries, interisland transportation and access to healthcare can influence your household budget.

When evaluating employment opportunities, compare estimated net income alongside employer-provided accommodation, transportation benefits, insurance coverage and retirement contributions.

For example, an employer that covers your full disability insurance and healthcare premium may provide a more valuable compensation package than a similar employer requiring larger employee contributions.

Calculate the estimated take-home pay for each job before assessing the overall financial differences.

## Planning Your Hawaii Monthly Budget

Use your net income to establish spending limits for housing, food, transportation, utilities and other essential expenses.

If you work in an industry with seasonal demand, avoid assuming that your highest-earning paycheck represents your normal income.

Our [emergency fund calculator](/savings/emergency-fund-calculator/) can help you establish a savings target based on monthly expenses. Our [salary-to-hourly calculator](/calculators/salary-to-hourly-calculator/) can help you compare fixed salaries with hourly employment.

Review your paycheck whenever Hawaii updates its withholding schedules or your employer modifies its insurance arrangements.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is the maximum Hawaii TDI deduction in 2026?

The maximum standard employee deduction is $7.50 per week. It also cannot exceed 0.5% of weekly wages or half the applicable premium cost.

### Does every Hawaii employee pay the same healthcare deduction?

No. Employee healthcare deductions depend on coverage, eligibility, earnings, premium costs and employer contributions. Ordinary required employee coverage is subject to statutory cost-sharing limits.

### Why did my Hawaii paycheck change even though my salary stayed the same?

Changes to state withholding schedules, federal tax rules, employee benefits, insurance premiums or payroll contribution limits can affect take-home earnings without changing gross salary.
